rationale:
Split into three reusable obligations. Together they prove steps 1–3 of the supplied proof, and the parent keeps only steps 4–5. The theorem is not atomic: it combines a calculus identity, a closure property of test forms, a current identity and a measure-theoretic estimate. The first three are standard facts that cutoff arguments elsewhere in the slicing branch also need.

The children:
(1) leibniz, cmcs_cd_extDeriv_smul_leibniz. The pointwise Leibniz rule d(gη)(x) = g(x)·dη(x) + alternatizeUncurryFin((Dg(x)).smulRight(η(x))), the last term being dg∧η, for Mathlib's extDeriv. Mathlib 25730c7c has only the constant-scalar extDeriv_smul and extDeriv_fun_smul; SimonGMT has nothing.
(2) smul_test_form, cmcs_cd_smul_mem_testFormOn. 𝒟ⁿ(U) is closed under multiplication by C^∞ functions. SimonGMT's testFormOnSubmodule gives closure under constants only. (3) uses this lemma twice, at degrees k and k+1.
(3) defect_identity, cmcs_cd_defect_identity. Simon 6.4.11's identity T(g dη) − ∂T(gη) = −T(dg∧η), written through the two integral representations. It assumes no integrability and does not need the hypothesis |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|. It depends on (1) and (2).

How the children prove the selected parent (steps 4–5 of the supplied proof):
- Rewrite with (3) and then abs_neg. The left side becomes ofReal|∫ ξ(x)(D(x)) dμ|, with D(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight(η̂ x)).
- ofReal|∫G dμ| = ‖∫G dμ‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖G‖ₑ dμ, by Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs and enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm. This holds even when G is not integrable.
- Apply lintegral_mono_ae with the μ-a.e. bound ‖ξ(x)(D(x))‖ₑ = ofReal|ξ(x)(D(x))| ≤ ofReal(‖Dg(x)‖·|η̂(x)|). The bound follows from the hypothesis on ξ, the sibling cmcs_wedge_norm_le (the parent's existing dependency wedge_norm-a1, already in its depends_on) and ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal.

subproblems.title: Leibniz rule for the exterior derivative of a function times a form: d(gη) = g dη + dg∧η
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) (x : Euclid P), DifferentiableAt ℝ g x → DifferentiableAt ℝ η x → exteriorDerivative (fun y => g y • η y) x = g x • exteriorDerivative η x + ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.11 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1378–1386). Its middle step T(γ∘f dω) − T(d(γ∘f ω)) = −T(γ'(f) df ∧ ω) rests on the Leibniz expansion d(γ∘f·ω) = γ∘f·dω + d(γ∘f) ∧ ω. This is step 1 (Leibniz rule) of the parent proof of cmcs_cutoff_defect_bound, isolated for an arbitrary function g and an arbitrary k-form η that are differentiable at the point x.

Notation: A := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin. For a k-form θ : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) k (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k), SimonGMT's exteriorDerivative θ is an abbreviation (abbrev) of Mathlib's extDeriv θ, and Mathlib defines extDeriv θ x := A (fderiv ℝ θ x).

1. (Unfold the definitions.) By the two definitions just recalled, exteriorDerivative (fun y => g y • η y) x is definitionally A (fderiv ℝ (fun y => g y • η y) x), and exteriorDerivative η x is definitionally A (fderiv ℝ η x). So the claim is definitionally the equation
   A (fderiv ℝ (fun y => g y • η y) x) = g x • A (fderiv ℝ η x) + A ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x)).
   In Lean, change the goal to this form with `show`.
2. (Product rule.) Let hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g x and hη : DifferentiableAt ℝ η x be the two hypotheses. Mathlib's product rule for a scalar function times a vector-valued function, fderiv_fun_smul hg hη, gives
   fderiv ℝ (fun y => g y • η y) x = g x • fderiv ℝ η x + (fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x).
   Here (fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x) is the continuous linear map v ↦ (fderiv ℝ g x v) • η x.
3. (Linearity of A.) A is the continuous linear map alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ applied to its argument. So A is additive: A (F + G) = A F + A G (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_add). It also commutes with real scalars: A (c • F) = c • A F (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul, used with c = g x).
4. (Conclusion.) Rewrite the left side of the goal of step 1 by step 2, then by the additivity of step 3, and finally by the homogeneity of step 3 at c = g x:
   A (g x • fderiv ℝ η x + (fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x)) = A (g x • fderiv ℝ η x) + A ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x)) = g x • A (fderiv ℝ η x) + A ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x)).
   This is the right side of the goal. In Lean, after the `show` of step 1, `rw [fderiv_fun_smul hg hη, ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_add, ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul]` closes the goal (checked against Mathlib 25730c7c). ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold exteriorDerivative = extDeriv: exteriorDerivative θ x is definitionally alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ θ x); reduce the goal with `show`.
Product rule fderiv_fun_smul hg hη: fderiv ℝ (fun y => g y • η y) x = g x • fderiv ℝ η x + (fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x).
alternatizeUncurryFin is additive and ℝ-homogeneous (alternatizeUncurryFin_add, alternatizeUncurryFin_smul); rewriting with both closes the goal.

subproblems.title: Test forms in U are closed under multiplication by C^∞ functions
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ∞ g), and let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n. Thus ω is a C^∞ n-form on ℝ^P whose topological support is compact and contained in U. Then the n-form x ↦ g(x)·ω(x) also belongs to 𝒟ⁿ(U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (ω : TestFormOn U n), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → (fun x => g x • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∈ TestFormOn U n
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof of cmcs_cutoff_defect_bound: the forms g·η and g·dη are test forms in U, being smooth and vanishing wherever η, resp. dη, vanishes. Here the step is isolated for an arbitrary test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). This is the C^∞-multiplier property of 𝒟ⁿ(U) that Simon 4.11 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1378–1386) uses implicitly when it evaluates T on γ∘f·dω and on d(γ∘f·ω).

Notation: ω̂ := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) is the underlying form of ω, and θ := (fun x => g x • ω̂ x). Let hg : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g be the hypothesis.

1. (What membership means.) TestFormOn U n is an abbreviation for the submodule testFormOnSubmodule U n of DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n. Its carrier is {θ | IsTestForm θ ∧ tsupport θ ⊆ U}. By the SimonGMT definitions:
   - IsTestForm θ = IsSmoothForm θ ∧ HasCompactSupport θ;
   - IsSmoothForm θ = ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ, where ∞ = ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞). This is exactly the smoothness order of the hypothesis ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g;
   - HasCompactSupport θ = IsCompact (tsupport θ).
   Hence θ ∈ TestFormOn U n follows from (a) ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) θ, (b) IsCompact (tsupport θ), and (c) tsupport θ ⊆ U, via the anonymous constructor ⟨⟨(a), (b)⟩, (c)⟩. Applied to ω itself, ω.property : IsTestForm ω̂ ∧ tsupport ω̂ ⊆ U gives three facts: ω̂ is C^∞ (ω.property.1.1), tsupport ω̂ is compact (ω.property.1.2), and tsupport ω̂ ⊆ U (ω.property.2).
2. (Smoothness, (a).) θ is the pointwise scalar product of the C^∞ real function g with the C^∞ map ω̂. The map ω̂ takes values in the normed space Covector (Euclid P) n of continuous alternating maps. Scalar multiplication ℝ × Covector (Euclid P) n → Covector (Euclid P) n is continuous and bilinear, so θ is C^∞. In Mathlib this is ContDiff.smul applied to hg and ω.property.1.1.
3. (Support inclusion.) If ω̂ x = 0, then θ x = g x • 0 = 0. So support θ ⊆ support ω̂, and taking closures gives tsupport θ ⊆ tsupport ω̂ (Mathlib: tsupport_smul_subset_right (fun x => g x) ω̂).
4. (Compactness, (b).) tsupport θ is closed (isClosed_tsupport θ). By step 3 it is contained in the compact set tsupport ω̂. A closed subset of a compact set is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), so tsupport θ is compact. Implementation note: prove (b) exactly this way. Applying HasCompactSupport.smul_left to a goal written as HasCompactSupport (fun x => g x • ω̂ x) hit a whnf heartbeat timeout in testing.
5. (Support in U, (c).) By step 3 and step 1, tsupport θ ⊆ tsupport ω̂ ⊆ U.
6. (Conclusion.) Steps 2, 4 and 5 give (a), (b) and (c), so θ ∈ TestFormOn U n by step 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Membership in TestFormOn U n unfolds to (ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ ∧ IsCompact (tsupport θ)) ∧ tsupport θ ⊆ U; ω.property gives the three facts for ω̂.
θ = g·ω̂ is C^∞ by ContDiff.smul.
tsupport θ ⊆ tsupport ω̂ by tsupport_smul_subset_right.
tsupport θ is a closed subset of the compact set tsupport ω̂, hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), and tsupport θ ⊆ tsupport ω̂ ⊆ U.

subproblems.title: Simon's identity 4.11 via integral representations: T(g dη) − ∂T(gη) = −T(dg∧η)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set. Let T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (k+1)) and let μ, μ' be measures on ℝ^P. Let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{k+1}(ℝ^P) and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) take values in the continuous linear functionals on covectors (MultiVector). Assume:
- T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U);
- ∂T(θ) = ∫ ξ'(x)(θ(x)) dμ'(x) for all θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U).
Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ and η ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Then, as real numbers (Bochner integrals, with no integrability assumed),
∫ g(x)·ξ(x)(dη(x)) dμ(x) − ∫ g(x)·ξ'(x)(η(x)) dμ'(x) = −∫ ξ(x)(alternatizeUncurryFin((Dg(x)).smulRight(η(x)))) dμ(x),
where dη = exteriorDerivative η and Dg(x) = fderiv ℝ g x. Informally: T(g dη) − ∂T(gη) = −T(dg∧η).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (k + 1)) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P k) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (η : TestFormOn U k), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (k + 1), T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ θ : TestFormOn U k, T.boundary θ = ∫ x, ξ' x ((θ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ') → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → ∫ x, g x * ξ x (exteriorDerivative (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ - ∫ x, g x * ξ' x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ' = -∫ x, ξ x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x))) ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.11 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1378–1386): ∂(T⌞γ∘f)(ω) − (∂T)⌞γ∘f(ω) = T(γ∘f dω) − T(d(γ∘f ω)) = −T(γ'(f) df ∧ ω). The same identity is proved here with two changes: an arbitrary C^∞ function g replaces γ∘f, and T and ∂T are written through their integral representations. These are steps 1–3 of the parent proof of cmcs_cutoff_defect_bound.

Sibling lemmas used:
- cmcs_cd_extDeriv_smul_leibniz: for all P, k, g : Euclid P → ℝ, η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k and x such that g and η are differentiable at x, exteriorDerivative (fun y => g y • η y) x = g x • exteriorDerivative η x + ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x)).
- cmcs_cd_smul_mem_testFormOn: for all P, n, U, g and ω : TestFormOn U n with ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g, (fun x => g x • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∈ TestFormOn U n.

No integrability is used. Every equality of integrals below comes from one of two sources:
- a pointwise equality of integrands, via integral_congr_ae, which holds for arbitrary functions;
- one of the representation hypotheses.

Notation:
- η̂ := (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) and dη̂ := exteriorDerivative η̂;
- D(x) := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η̂ x)), a (k+1)-covector;
- hT and hbT are the representation hypotheses of T and of T.boundary, and hg is the smoothness of g.

1. (Test forms.) Define:
   - dη := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k η ∈ TestFormOn U (k+1). By definition of exteriorDerivativeTestOn, its underlying form is dη̂.
   - η_g := ⟨fun x => g x • η̂ x, cmcs_cd_smul_mem_testFormOn P k U g η hg⟩ ∈ TestFormOn U k.
   - ω_g := ⟨fun x => g x • (dη : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k+1)) x, cmcs_cd_smul_mem_testFormOn P (k+1) U g dη hg⟩ ∈ TestFormOn U (k+1). Its underlying form is x ↦ g x • dη̂ x.
   - dη_g := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k η_g ∈ TestFormOn U (k+1). Its underlying form is exteriorDerivative (fun y => g y • η̂ y).
   - D_T := dη_g − ω_g ∈ TestFormOn U (k+1), a difference in the submodule. Its underlying form is the pointwise difference of the two underlying forms.
2. (The first integral is T ω_g.) For each x, ξ x is ℝ-linear, so ξ x (g x • dη̂ x) = g x * ξ x (dη̂ x) (map_smul, smul_eq_mul). Hence the integrands x ↦ g x * ξ x (dη̂ x) and x ↦ ξ x ((ω_g : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k+1)) x) agree at every x. By integral_congr_ae and hT ω_g:
   ∫ g x * ξ x (dη̂ x) dμ = ∫ ξ x (ω_g x) dμ = T ω_g.
3. (The second integral is T dη_g.) Likewise ξ' x (g x • η̂ x) = g x * ξ' x (η̂ x) for every x. By integral_congr_ae and hbT η_g:
   ∫ g x * ξ' x (η̂ x) dμ' = ∫ ξ' x (η_g x) dμ' = T.boundary η_g = T dη_g.
   The last equality is GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply: T.boundary θ = T (exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k θ), which holds by rfl.
4. (Pointwise value of D_T.) Fix x.
   - g is differentiable at x because it is C^∞: hg.differentiable, with the side condition 1 ≤ ∞ closed by simp.
   - η̂ is differentiable at x because it is C^∞: η.property.1.1.differentiable, with the same side condition.
   - By cmcs_cd_extDeriv_smul_leibniz P k g η̂ x, exteriorDerivative (fun y => g y • η̂ y) x = g x • dη̂ x + D(x).
   Hence the underlying form of D_T at x is
   D_T(x) = exteriorDerivative (fun y => g y • η̂ y) x − g x • dη̂ x = D(x).
   In Lean, `change` the goal to this difference, rewrite with the Leibniz lemma, and close it with `abel`.
5. (Linearity of T.) T acts through the ℝ-linear map T.toCurrent : TestFormOn U (k+1) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ. So T D_T = T(dη_g − ω_g) = T dη_g − T ω_g, that is, T ω_g − T dη_g = −T D_T. Implementation note: after `change` to T.toCurrent, use `LinearMap.map_sub (T.toCurrent : ↥(TestFormOn U (k + 1)) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k η_g) ω_g` and finish with `ring`. A bare `rw [map_sub]` or `simp only [map_sub]` failed to match in testing.
6. (T D_T as an integral.) By hT D_T, T D_T = ∫ ξ x (D_T x) dμ. By step 4 (via congrArg (ξ x)) and integral_congr_ae, this equals ∫ ξ x (D(x)) dμ.
7. (Conclusion.) Steps 2, 3, 5 and 6 give
   ∫ g x * ξ x (dη̂ x) dμ − ∫ g x * ξ' x (η̂ x) dμ' = T ω_g − T dη_g = −T D_T = −∫ ξ x (D(x)) dμ,
   which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Build η_g = gη ∈ 𝒟^k(U) and ω_g = g dη ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U) with cmcs_cd_smul_mem_testFormOn; set dη_g := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k η_g and D_T := dη_g − ω_g.
Linearity of ξ(x) and ξ'(x), integral_congr_ae and the two representations give ∫ g ξ(dη) dμ = T(ω_g) and ∫ g ξ'(η) dμ' = ∂T(η_g) = T(dη_g).
By cmcs_cd_extDeriv_smul_leibniz, D_T(x) = d(gη)(x) − g(x)dη(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin((Dg(x)).smulRight(η(x))) for every x.
Linearity of T (LinearMap.map_sub on T.toCurrent) gives T(ω_g) − T(dη_g) = −T(D_T); by the representation of T and step 3 this is −∫ ξ(D) dμ.
